# Full analysis script

This workflow follows the corrected R script, including the additional breakpoint parameter in AIC comparisons. Statistical TXT and CSV outputs are saved in the Mark_Down folder, as in the reference R Markdown workflow. Figure output paths are preserved.

```{r markdown-output-setup, include=FALSE}
dir.create("/Users/bz294/Documents/WhiteZone/Figure/Backup/Mark_Down", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## 1. Setting up

```{r 1-setting-up}
# Section 1 - Setting up
get_directory <- function() {
  args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = FALSE)
  file <- "--file="
  rstudio <- "RStudio"
  
  match <- grep(rstudio, args)
  if (length(match) > 0) {
    return(dirname(rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path))
  } else {
    match <- grep(file, args)
    if (length(match) > 0) {
      return(dirname(normalizePath(sub(file, "", args[match]))))
    } else {
      return(dirname(normalizePath(sys.frames()[[1]]$ofile)))
    }
  }
}

path <- if (isTRUE(getOption("knitr.in.progress"))) {
  dirname(normalizePath(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)))
} else {
  get_directory()
} ## get current directory path
setwd(path)
source( './function_MakeVegetationZoneLayers.R')
source( './function_Make_TransectLayers.R')
source( './function_called_by_main_script.R')

rast.files <- list.files(
  path = '/Volumes/MaloneLab/Research/Whitezone/Result/Emulation/Final/Roy',
  pattern = "^raster.*\\.tif$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

```

## 2. Raster stack and transects

```{r 2-raster-transects}
# Section 2 - Read in raster stack and transects
# Section 2.1 - read in raster stack
setwd( '/Volumes/MaloneLab/Research/Whitezone/Result/Emulation/Final/Roy')

coast <- rast(rast.files) %>%
  terra::project("+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84", method = "near") ## "near to make sure class value is not interpolated "
terra::time(coast) <-  substr(rast.files, 8, 11) %>% as.numeric # get the time out of the list of file names

ENP.transects <- makeTransect(line1 = coast.sf, line2 =  inland.sf, transect.n= 100)
# Calculate the centroid of each transect
ENP.transects <- ENP.transects %>%
  mutate(centroid = st_centroid(st_geometry(.)))

cent_coords <- st_coordinates(ENP.transects$centroid)

# Extract latitude and longitude from the centroid
ENP.transects <- ENP.transects %>%
  mutate(
    lon = cent_coords[, 1],
    lat = cent_coords[, 2]
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-centroid)  # remove if centroid is not needed

```

## 3. Land cover proportion data and transects

```{r 3-land-cover-data}
# Section 3 Prepare the land-cover proportion data (summary_data_df) and transects
# load the results, instead of running the four steps above. 
# load("/Volumes/Malonelab/Research/Whitezone/Result/Spatial_Modelling/results.RData")

load("/Volumes/Malonelab/Research/Whitezone/Result/Spatial_Modelling/results_Roy.RData")
# Section 3.1: Combine all land cover change data into one data frame
summary_data_df <- do.call(rbind, results)
summary_data_df$year <- as.double(summary_data_df$year)
colnames(summary_data_df) <- c("ID", "time", "proportion_Int1", "proportion_Int2", "proportion_Int3")

# Section 3.2 extract transects
```

## 4. Transect change rates

```{r 4-change-rates}


# ============================================================
# SECTION 4. LANDSCAPE-WIDE DZ AND VZ TRANSECT CHANGE RATES
# Study period: 1984–2024 (40 years)
#
# Outputs:
# 1. Individual transect change rates (m/yr)
# 2. Landscape-wide DZ mean, SD, and median
# 3. Landscape-wide VZ mean, SD, and median
# 4. Transect rate shapefile
# 5. Landscape summary CSV
#
# No salinity models or regional statistical comparisons.
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(sf)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4.1. OUTPUT DIRECTORY
# ------------------------------------------------------------

output_dir <- "/Users/bz294/Documents/WhiteZone/Figure/Backup/Mark_Down"

dir.create(
  output_dir,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4.2. CALCULATE LAND-COVER PROPORTION CHANGES
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Use the 1984 and 2024 observations for each transect.

temp <- summary_data_df %>%
  filter(time %in% c(1984, 2024)) %>%
  arrange(ID, time) %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  filter(
    any(time == 1984),
    any(time == 2024)
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    trend_Int1 =
      proportion_Int1[time == 2024][1] -
      proportion_Int1[time == 1984][1],

    trend_Int2 =
      proportion_Int2[time == 2024][1] -
      proportion_Int2[time == 1984][1],

    trend_Int3 =
      proportion_Int3[time == 2024][1] -
      proportion_Int3[time == 1984][1],

    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4.3. CONVERT PROPORTION CHANGES TO SPATIAL RATES
# ------------------------------------------------------------

rate_results <- transects_in_polygon %>%
  mutate(
    length.org = as.numeric(length.org)
  ) %>%
  left_join(temp, by = "ID") %>%
  mutate(
    length_change_Int1 =
      length.org * trend_Int1 / 40,

    length_change_Int2 =
      length.org * trend_Int2 / 40,

    length_change_Int3 =
      length.org * trend_Int3 / 40
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4.4. EXPORT SPATIAL TRANSECT DATA
# ------------------------------------------------------------

output_path <- paste0(
  "/Volumes/MaloneLab/Research/Whitezone/",
  "Result/Spatial_Modelling/",
  "transects_with_trend_.shp"
)

st_write(
  rate_results,
  output_path,
  delete_layer = TRUE
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4.5. PLOT TRANSECT RATES
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# DZ rates
result <- plot_rates(
  rate_results,
  length_col = "length_change_Int2"
)

rescaled_transects <- result$transects
connection_line <- result$connection_line

# VZ rates
result_vz <- plot_rates(
  rate_results,
  length_col = "length_change_Int1"
)

rescaled_vz <- result_vz$transects

# Preserve original spatial summaries
calculate_length_change_averages(
  rate_results,
  "length_change_Int2",
  custom_range = c(27, 37)
)

calculate_length_change_averages(
  rate_results,
  "length_change_Int1",
  custom_range = c(27, 37)
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4.6. PREPARE UNIQUE TRANSECTS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

rates <- rate_results %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  distinct(ID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(ID >= 1 & ID <= 100)

cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("NUMBER OF TRANSECTS\n")
cat("========================================\n")

print(nrow(rates))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4.7. LANDSCAPE-WIDE DZ AND VZ RATE STATISTICS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

rate_long <- bind_rows(
  rates %>%
    transmute(
      ID,
      Zone = "DZ",
      rate = as.numeric(length_change_Int2)
    ),
  rates %>%
    transmute(
      ID,
      Zone = "VZ",
      rate = as.numeric(length_change_Int1)
    )
) %>%
  filter(is.finite(rate))


# ============================================================
# WELCH ANOVA + GAMES-HOWELL
# DZ and VZ transect rates, 1984–2024
# LAND-COVER DATA ONLY (NO SALINITY)
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(rstatix)

# 1. Assign subregions using transect IDs
rate_test_data <- rate_long %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    region = case_when(
      ID >= 62 & ID <= 100 ~ "Western",
      ID >= 37 & ID <= 61  ~ "Central",
      ID >= 1  & ID <= 36  ~ "Eastern",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(region),
    Zone %in% c("DZ", "VZ"),
    is.finite(rate)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    region = factor(
      region,
      levels = c("Western", "Central", "Eastern")
    )
  )

# 2. Check sample sizes
print(rate_test_data %>% count(Zone, region))

# 3. Overall Welch ANOVA
overall_results <- rate_test_data %>%
  group_by(Zone) %>%
  welch_anova_test(rate ~ region)

print(overall_results, n = Inf)

# 4. Pairwise Games–Howell tests
pairwise_results <- rate_test_data %>%
  group_by(Zone) %>%
  games_howell_test(rate ~ region)

print(pairwise_results, n = Inf)

# 5. Export results
output_dir <- "/Users/bz294/Documents/WhiteZone/Figure/Backup/Mark_Down"

dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

write.csv(
  overall_results,
  file.path(output_dir, "Rate_Welch_ANOVA.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  pairwise_results,
  file.path(output_dir, "Rate_Games_Howell.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

landscape_results <- rate_long %>%
  group_by(Zone) %>%
  summarise(
    Region = "Landscape",
    n = n(),
    mean_rate_m_yr = mean(rate),
    sd_rate_m_yr = sd(rate),
    median_rate_m_yr = median(rate),
    min_rate_m_yr = min(rate),
    max_rate_m_yr = max(rate),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(factor(Zone, levels = c("DZ", "VZ")))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4.8. PRINT LANDSCAPE RESULTS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("LANDSCAPE-WIDE TRANSECT CHANGE RATES\n")
cat("Study period: 1984–2024\n")
cat("Units: m/yr\n")
cat("========================================\n")

print(landscape_results, n = Inf)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4.9. EXPORT LANDSCAPE RESULTS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

write.csv(
  landscape_results,
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    "Landscape_transect_rates.csv"
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Export individual transect rates
write.csv(
  rate_long,
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    "Individual_transect_rates.csv"
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("LANDSCAPE ANALYSIS COMPLETED\n")
cat("========================================\n")

cat(
  "\nResults saved to:\n",
  file.path(output_dir, "Landscape_transect_rates.csv"),
  "\n"
)


# ============================================================
# LANDSCAPE + SUBREGIONAL TRANSECT RATE RESULTS
# Run after rate_results has been calculated
# ============================================================

output_dir <- "/Users/bz294/Documents/WhiteZone/Figure/Backup/Mark_Down"
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Prepare individual transect rates
rates <- rate_results %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  distinct(ID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    region = case_when(
      ID >= 62 & ID <= 100 ~ "Western",
      ID >= 37 & ID <= 61 ~ "Central",
      ID >= 1  & ID <= 36 ~ "Eastern",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(region))

rate_long <- bind_rows(
  rates %>%
    transmute(ID, region, Zone = "DZ",
              rate = as.numeric(length_change_Int2)),
  rates %>%
    transmute(ID, region, Zone = "VZ",
              rate = as.numeric(length_change_Int1))
) %>%
  filter(is.finite(rate))

# Subregional results
regional_results <- rate_long %>%
  group_by(Zone, region) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_rate_m_yr = mean(rate),
    sd_rate_m_yr = sd(rate),
    median_rate_m_yr = median(rate),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Landscape-wide results
landscape_results <- rate_long %>%
  group_by(Zone) %>%
  summarise(
    region = "Landscape",
    n = n(),
    mean_rate_m_yr = mean(rate),
    sd_rate_m_yr = sd(rate),
    median_rate_m_yr = median(rate),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Welch ANOVA
anova_results <- rate_long %>%
  group_by(Zone) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    test <- oneway.test(rate ~ region, data = .x,
                        var.equal = FALSE)
    tibble(
      regional_difference_p = test$p.value,
      significant_difference =
        ifelse(test$p.value < 0.05, "Yes", "No")
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

regional_results <- regional_results %>%
  left_join(anova_results, by = "Zone")

landscape_results <- landscape_results %>%
  mutate(
    regional_difference_p = NA_real_,
    significant_difference = NA_character_
  )

# Combine all 8 rows
table_results <- bind_rows(
  landscape_results,
  regional_results
) %>%
  mutate(
    Zone = factor(Zone, levels = c("DZ", "VZ")),
    region = factor(
      region,
      levels = c("Landscape", "Western", "Central", "Eastern")
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(Zone, region)

print(table_results, n = Inf)

# Export combined results
write.csv(
  table_results,
  file.path(output_dir, "Transect_rate_table_results.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Export landscape separately
write.csv(
  landscape_results,
  file.path(output_dir, "Landscape_transect_rates.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat("\nAll landscape and subregional results saved.\n")





```

## 6. Salinity and mixed effects models

```{r 6-salinity}
# Section 6 - processing salinity data (Fig. 7)
# Section 6.1 read in the salinity data
salinity_data <- read.csv("/Volumes/MaloneLab/Research/Whitezone/Hydro_Salinity/Salinity/salinity_annual_avg_full.csv")
selected_sites <- c(
  "FLAB12_salinity",
  "FLAB11_salinity",
  "FLAB10_salinity",
  "ENPTR_salinity",
  "ENPLM_salinity",
  "ENPTC_salinity",
  "FLAB08_salinity",
  "FLAB07_salinity",
  "ENPDK_salinity",
  "ENPBS_salinity",
  "ENPLB_salinity",
  "ENPLS_salinity",
  "ENPHC_salinity",
  "FLAB04_salinity"
)

all_site_names <- salinity_data$site[salinity_data$site %in% selected_sites]

# Section 6.2: Filter summary_data_df for the years that match
matching_years <- salinity_data$year  ## 1991 onwards 
summary_data <- summary_data_df %>%
  filter(time %in% matching_years)
summary_data$time <- as.double(summary_data$time)

# 6.3 Assign the sites to a region (west, central, and east)
west <- c(
  "FLAB12_salinity",
  "FLAB11_salinity",
  "FLAB10_salinity",
  "ENPTR_salinity",
  "ENPLM_salinity",
  "ENPTC_salinity"
)

central <- c(
  "FLAB08_salinity",
  "FLAB07_salinity",
  "ENPDK_salinity",
  "ENPBS_salinity",
  "ENPLB_salinity",
  "ENPLS_salinity",
  "ENPHC_salinity"
)

east <- c(
  "FLAB04_salinity"
)

salinity_data <- salinity_data %>%
  mutate(
    subregion = case_when(
      site %in% west ~ "West",
      site %in% central ~ "Central",
      site %in% east ~ "East",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# Section 6.2 Calculate correlations by region
correlation_salinity_dz_detrended <-
  compute_detrended_correlations_by_region(
    all_annual_averages = salinity_data,
    summary_data = summary_data,
    west_sites = west,
    central_sites = central,
    east_sites = east,
    proportion_col = "proportion_Int2"
  )

head(correlation_salinity_dz_detrended)

# Section 6.3 Join with the lat and lon info
csv_file <- "/Volumes/Malonelab/Research/Whitezone/Hydro_Salinity/Salinity/WZ_salinity_sites_latlon.csv"  # replace with your file path
salinity_summary <- read.csv(csv_file)
salinity_summary <- na.omit(salinity_summary)  # Remove rows with N/A values

# Assuming the 2nd and 3rd columns are Lat and Lon in DDMMSS.SS format
salinity_summary <- salinity_summary %>% ## this data is the records for salinity and lat/lon
  mutate(
    lat_decimal = sapply(salinity_summary[[3]], convert_to_decimal),  # Convert lat to decimal degrees
    lon_decimal = sapply(salinity_summary[[4]], convert_to_decimal)  # Convert lon to decimal degrees
  )
salinity_summary$lon_decimal <- -abs(salinity_summary$lon_decimal)
export_flab_stations(salinity_summary, '/Volumes/MaloneLab/Research/Whitezone/Result/Spatial_Modelling/Results/')

# 6.4 Plot DZ correlation with salinity based on rates
# Join correlation to the transects
rescaled_transects_colored <- rescaled_transects %>%
  left_join(correlation_salinity_dz_detrended, by = "ID")

# Extract coordinates
rescaled_coords_dz <- st_coordinates(rescaled_transects_colored) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Now bind attributes back from the sf object
rescaled_coords_dz <- rescaled_coords_dz %>%
  dplyr::mutate(row_id = L1) %>%   # match rows to features
  dplyr::left_join(
    rescaled_transects_colored %>% 
      tibble::rowid_to_column("row_id") %>%   # row_id aligns with L1
      st_drop_geometry(),                     # drop geometry but keep attributes
    by = "row_id"
  )

transect_plot_dz <- ggplot() +
  geom_path(
    data = rescaled_coords_dz,
    aes(X, Y, group = ID, color = correlation),
    linewidth = 3
  ) +
  geom_sf(data = connection_line, color = "black", linewidth = 2) +
  geom_sf(
    data = subset_transects_utm,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 3,
    linetype = "11"
  ) +
  scale_color_gradientn(
    colors = c("#c6dbef", "#6baed6", "#08519c"),
    values = scales::rescale(c(-0.6, 0, 0.6)),
    limits = c(-0.6, 0.6),
    breaks = c(-0.6, -0.3, 0, 0.3, 0.6),
    oob = scales::squish,
    na.value = "grey80",
    name = "Correlation"
  ) +
  coord_sf(datum = NA, expand = FALSE) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
# white backgrounds
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    
# remove grids
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    
# remove axes
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_blank(),
    
# remove border
    panel.border = element_blank(),
    
# legend
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 18, family = "Times"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 18, family = "Times"),
    legend.key.height = unit(1.2, "cm"),
    legend.key.width = unit(0.5, "cm")
  ) +
  guides(
    color = guide_colorbar(
      direction = "horizontal",
      title.position = "top",
      barwidth = unit(15, "cm"),
      barheight = unit(0.8, "cm")
    )
  )

ggsave(
  filename = "/Users/bz294/Documents/WhiteZone/Figure/Backup/rescaled_dz_plot_roy_detrended.tif",
  plot = transect_plot_dz,   # use the named plot object
  device = "tiff",
  width = 10,
  height = 8,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"            # ensures white background
)

landscape_results <- list()

for (zone in c("DZ", "VZ")) {

  response <- if (zone == "DZ") {
    "proportion_Int2"
  } else {
    "proportion_Int1"
  }

  dat <- mixed_data %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[response]])) %>%
    droplevels()

  # One common slope across the entire SESE
  # Retain region as an adjustment for baseline differences
  formula_landscape <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      response,
      " ~ salinity_c + year_c + region + ",
      "(1 | ID) + (1 | RegionYear) + ",
      "ar1(year_f + 0 | ID)"
    )
  )

  model <- glmmTMB(
    formula_landscape,
    data = dat,
    family = gaussian()
  )

  coefs <- summary(model)$coefficients$cond

  # Convert proportion units to percentage points
  out <- data.frame(
    Zone = zone,
    N = nobs(model),
    Annual_rate = 100 * coefs["year_c", "Estimate"],
    Annual_p = coefs["year_c", "Pr(>|z|)"],
    Salinity_slope = 100 * coefs["salinity_c", "Estimate"],
    Salinity_p = coefs["salinity_c", "Pr(>|z|)"]
  )

  landscape_results[[zone]] <- out
}

)
```

## 8. VZ threshold analysis

```{r 8-vz-threshold}
# Threshold analysis for vz
# 1. Prepare VZ data

vz_data <- mixed_data %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(proportion_Int1),
    !is.na(salinity),
    !is.na(year),
    !is.na(ID)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ID = factor(ID),
    year_f = factor(year),
    year_c = year - mean(year, na.rm = TRUE)
  )


# 2. Define candidate salinity thresholds
# Avoid extreme tails because there may be too few observations
# on one side of the breakpoint.

candidate_thresholds <- seq(
  quantile(vz_data$salinity, 0.10, na.rm = TRUE),
  quantile(vz_data$salinity, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE),
  by = 0.25
)

candidate_thresholds
# 3. Fit threshold models
# Model:
# VZ = b0 + b1*salinity + b2*(salinity-threshold)+ + ...
# Below threshold:
# slope = b1
# Above threshold:
# slope = b1 + b2

results <- data.frame(
  threshold = candidate_thresholds,
  AIC = NA_real_
)

models <- vector("list", length(candidate_thresholds))


for (i in seq_along(candidate_thresholds)) {
  
  bp <- candidate_thresholds[i]
  
  cat(
    "Fitting model",
    i, "of", length(candidate_thresholds),
    "| threshold =", round(bp, 2), "PSU\n"
  )
  
  flush.console()
  
  dat <- vz_data %>%
    mutate(
      salinity_bp = salinity - bp,
      post_threshold = pmax(0, salinity - bp)
    )
  
  mod <- glmmTMB(
    proportion_Int1 ~
      salinity_bp +
      post_threshold +
      year_c +
      (1 | ID) +
      (1 | RegionYear) +
      ar1(year_f + 0 | ID),
    data = dat,
    family = gaussian()
  )
  
  models[[i]] <- mod
  results$AIC[i] <- AIC(mod)
  
  cat("   AIC =", round(results$AIC[i], 2), "\n")
  flush.console()
}

results <- results %>%
  mutate(
    delta_AIC = AIC - min(AIC)
  ) %>%
  arrange(AIC)

results
best_threshold <- results$threshold[1]

best_threshold

best_index <- which(candidate_thresholds == best_threshold)

best_model <- models[[best_index]]

summary(best_model)
# SAVE ALL THRESHOLD ANALYSIS RESULTS TO A TEXT FILE

output_file <- "/Users/bz294/Documents/WhiteZone/Figure/Backup/Mark_Down/VZ_threshold_analysis_results.txt"

sink(output_file)

cat("============================================================\n")
cat("VZ-SALINITY THRESHOLD ANALYSIS\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")


# 1. Best threshold

cat("BEST THRESHOLD\n")
cat("------------------------------------------------------------\n")
cat("Best threshold =", best_threshold, "PSU\n\n")


# 2. All candidate thresholds and AIC

cat("ALL CANDIDATE THRESHOLDS\n")
cat("------------------------------------------------------------\n")
write.table(results, file = "", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
cat("\n\n")


# 3. Best model summary

cat("BEST THRESHOLD MODEL SUMMARY\n")
cat("------------------------------------------------------------\n")
print(summary(best_model))
cat("\n\n")


# 4. Fixed effects

cat("FIXED EFFECTS\n")
cat("------------------------------------------------------------\n")
print(fixef(best_model)$cond)
cat("\n\n")


# 5. Variance-covariance parameters

cat("VARIANCE / RANDOM EFFECT PARAMETERS\n")
cat("------------------------------------------------------------\n")
print(VarCorr(best_model))
cat("\n\n")


# 6. AIC of best threshold model

cat("BEST THRESHOLD MODEL AIC (INCLUDING BREAKPOINT)\n")
cat("------------------------------------------------------------\n")
print(AIC(best_model) + 2)
cat("\n\n")


# 7. Linear model for comparison

linear_model <- glmmTMB(
  proportion_Int1 ~
    salinity +
    year_c +

cat("------------------------------------------------------------\n")

cat("\n\n")


# 8. Linear vs threshold AIC

cat("LINEAR VS THRESHOLD MODEL AIC\n")
cat("------------------------------------------------------------\n")
aic_compare_initial <- AIC(linear_model, best_model)

# Count the estimated breakpoint as one additional parameter
aic_compare_initial$df[2] <- aic_compare_initial$df[2] + 1
aic_compare_initial$AIC[2] <- aic_compare_initial$AIC[2] + 2

write.table(aic_compare_initial, file = "", row.names = TRUE, quote = FALSE)

cat("\n")

cat(
  "AIC improvement (linear - threshold) =",
  aic_compare_initial$AIC[1] - aic_compare_initial$AIC[2],
  "\n\n"
)


# Close output file
```

## 9. Threshold slope estimates

```{r 9-threshold-slopes}
# Last analysis
# CALCULATE THRESHOLD SLOPES AND SAVE DIRECTLY TO TXT

# Extract coefficients and covariance matrix
b <- fixef(best_model)$cond
V <- vcov(best_model)$cond

# Function to calculate slope, SE, CI, z, and p
get_slope <- function(L, b, V) {
  
  est <- sum(L * b)
  
  se <- sqrt(
    as.numeric(t(L) %*% V %*% L)
  )
  
  z <- est / se
  p <- 2 * pnorm(abs(z), lower.tail = FALSE)
  
  data.frame(
    estimate = est,
    SE = se,
    lower95 = est - 1.96 * se,
    upper95 = est + 1.96 * se,
    z = z,
    p = p
  )
}


# BELOW-THRESHOLD SLOPE

L_below <- setNames(rep(0, length(b)), names(b))
L_below["salinity_bp"] <- 1

below <- get_slope(L_below, b, V)


# ABOVE-THRESHOLD SLOPE

L_above <- setNames(rep(0, length(b)), names(b))
L_above["salinity_bp"] <- 1
L_above["post_threshold"] <- 1

above <- get_slope(L_above, b, V)


# CHANGE IN SLOPE

L_change <- setNames(rep(0, length(b)), names(b))
L_change["post_threshold"] <- 1

change <- get_slope(L_change, b, V)


# CONVERT TO PERCENTAGE POINTS PER PSU

cols <- c("estimate", "SE", "lower95", "upper95")

below[cols] <- below[cols] * 100
above[cols] <- above[cols] * 100
change[cols] <- change[cols] * 100


# SAVE EVERYTHING TO FILE

output_file <- paste0(
  "/Users/bz294/Documents/WhiteZone/Figure/Backup/Mark_Down/",
  "VZ_threshold_slopes_results.txt"
)

con <- file(output_file, open = "wt")

writeLines(
  c(
    "============================================================",
    "VZ-SALINITY THRESHOLD SLOPE RESULTS",
    "============================================================",
    "",
    paste("Best threshold =", round(best_threshold, 4), "PSU"),
    ""
  ),
  con
)


writeLines(
  c(
    "------------------------------------------------------------",
    "BELOW-THRESHOLD SLOPE",
    paste("Salinity <", round(best_threshold, 4), "PSU"),
    "Units: VZ percentage points per PSU",
    "------------------------------------------------------------"
  ),
  con
)

write.table(
  below,
  file = con,
  row.names = FALSE,
  quote = FALSE
)


writeLines(
  c(
    "",
    "------------------------------------------------------------",
    "ABOVE-THRESHOLD SLOPE",
    paste("Salinity >", round(best_threshold, 4), "PSU"),
    "Units: VZ percentage points per PSU",
    "------------------------------------------------------------"
  ),
  con
)

write.table(
  above,
  file = con,
  row.names = FALSE,
  quote = FALSE
)


writeLines(
  c(
    "",
    "------------------------------------------------------------",
    "CHANGE IN SLOPE AT THRESHOLD",
    "Units: VZ percentage points per PSU",
    "------------------------------------------------------------"
  ),
  con
)

write.table(
  change,
  file = con,
  row.names = FALSE,
  quote = FALSE
)


writeLines(
  c(
    "",
    "------------------------------------------------------------",
    "MODEL INFORMATION",
    "------------------------------------------------------------",
    paste("Threshold model AIC (including breakpoint) =", AIC(best_model) + 2),
    paste("Number of observations =", nobs(best_model))
```

```{r 10-region-adjusted-threshold}
# 1. Candidate thresholds

candidate_thresholds_region <- seq(
  quantile(vz_region_data$salinity, 0.10, na.rm = TRUE),
  quantile(vz_region_data$salinity, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE),
  by = 0.25
)

region_results <- data.frame(
  threshold = candidate_thresholds_region,
  AIC = NA_real_
)

region_models <- vector(
  "list",
  length(candidate_thresholds_region)
)


# 2. Fit region-adjusted piecewise models
# Important:
# - region controls baseline differences
# - year_c * region allows regional temporal trends to differ
# - threshold effect is global across regions

for (i in seq_along(candidate_thresholds_region)) {
  
  bp <- candidate_thresholds_region[i]
  
  cat(
    "Region-adjusted model",
    i, "of", length(candidate_thresholds_region),
    "| threshold =", round(bp, 2), "PSU\n"
  )
  flush.console()
  
  dat_region <- vz_region_data %>%
    mutate(
      salinity_bp = salinity - bp,
      post_threshold = pmax(0, salinity - bp)
    )
  
  mod_region <- glmmTMB(
    proportion_Int1 ~
      salinity_bp +
      post_threshold +
      region +
      year_c * region +
      (1 | ID) +
      (1 | RegionYear) +
      ar1(year_f + 0 | ID),
    data = dat_region,
    family = gaussian()
  )
  
  region_models[[i]] <- mod_region
  region_results$AIC[i] <- AIC(mod_region)
  
  cat(
    "   AIC =",
    round(region_results$AIC[i], 2),
    "\n"
  )
  flush.console()
}


# 3. Identify best threshold

region_results <- region_results %>%
  mutate(
    delta_AIC = AIC - min(AIC)
  ) %>%
  arrange(AIC)

best_threshold_region <- region_results$threshold[1]

best_index_region <- which(
  candidate_thresholds_region == best_threshold_region
)

best_model_region <- region_models[[best_index_region]]


# 4. Equivalent REGION-ADJUSTED LINEAR model

linear_model_region <- glmmTMB(
  proportion_Int1 ~
    salinity +
    region +
    year_c * region +
    (1 | ID) +
    (1 | RegionYear) +
    ar1(year_f + 0 | ID),
  data = vz_region_data,
  family = gaussian()
)


# 5. Calculate below- and above-threshold slopes

b_region <- fixef(best_model_region)$cond
V_region <- vcov(best_model_region)$cond


get_slope_region <- function(L, b, V) {
  
  est <- sum(L * b)
  
  se <- sqrt(
    as.numeric(t(L) %*% V %*% L)
  )
  
  z <- est / se
  
  p <- 2 * pnorm(
    abs(z),
    lower.tail = FALSE
  )
  
  data.frame(
    estimate = est,
    SE = se,
    lower95 = est - 1.96 * se,
    upper95 = est + 1.96 * se,
    z = z,
    p = p
  )
}


# Below threshold
L_below_region <- setNames(
  rep(0, length(b_region)),
  names(b_region)
)

L_below_region["salinity_bp"] <- 1

below_region <- get_slope_region(
  L_below_region,
  b_region,
  V_region
)


# Above threshold
L_above_region <- setNames(
  rep(0, length(b_region)),
  names(b_region)
)

L_above_region["salinity_bp"] <- 1
L_above_region["post_threshold"] <- 1

above_region <- get_slope_region(
  L_above_region,
  b_region,
  V_region
)


# Change in slope
L_change_region <- setNames(
  rep(0, length(b_region)),
  names(b_region)
)

L_change_region["post_threshold"] <- 1

change_region <- get_slope_region(
  L_change_region,
  b_region,
  V_region
)


# Convert proportions to percentage points
cols <- c(
  "estimate",
  "SE",
  "lower95",
  "upper95"
)

below_region[cols] <- below_region[cols] * 100
above_region[cols] <- above_region[cols] * 100
change_region[cols] <- change_region[cols] * 100


# 6. Save EVERYTHING directly to TXT

output_region <- paste0(
  "/Users/bz294/Documents/WhiteZone/Figure/Backup/Mark_Down/",
  "VZ_threshold_region_adjusted_results.txt"
)

con <- file(
  output_region,
  open = "wt"
)


writeLines(
  c(
    "============================================================",
    "REGION-ADJUSTED VZ-SALINITY THRESHOLD ANALYSIS",
    "============================================================",
    "",
    paste(
      "Best threshold =",
      round(best_threshold_region, 4),
      "PSU"
    ),
    ""
  ),
  con
)


# AIC grid
writeLines(
  c(
    "------------------------------------------------------------",
    "ALL CANDIDATE THRESHOLDS",
    "------------------------------------------------------------"
  ),
  con
)

write.table(
  region_results,
  file = con,
  row.names = FALSE,
  quote = FALSE
)


# Best threshold model
writeLines(
  c(
    "",
    "",
    "------------------------------------------------------------",
    "BEST REGION-ADJUSTED THRESHOLD MODEL",
    "------------------------------------------------------------"
  ),
  con
)

capture.output(
  summary(best_model_region),
  file = con,
  append = TRUE
)


# Slopes
writeLines(
  c(
    "",
    "",
    "------------------------------------------------------------",
    "BELOW-THRESHOLD SLOPE",
    paste(
      "Salinity <",
      round(best_threshold_region, 4),
      "PSU"
    ),
    "Units: VZ percentage points per PSU",
    "------------------------------------------------------------"
  ),
  con
)

write.table(
  below_region,
  file = con,
  row.names = FALSE,
  quote = FALSE
)


writeLines(
  c(
    "",
    "------------------------------------------------------------",
    "ABOVE-THRESHOLD SLOPE",
    paste(
      "Salinity >",
      round(best_threshold_region, 4),
      "PSU"
    ),
    "Units: VZ percentage points per PSU",
    "------------------------------------------------------------"
  ),
  con
)

write.table(
  above_region,
  file = con,
  row.names = FALSE,
  quote = FALSE
)


writeLines(
  c(
    "",
    "------------------------------------------------------------",
    "CHANGE IN SLOPE AT THRESHOLD",
    "Units: VZ percentage points per PSU",
    "------------------------------------------------------------"
  ),
  con
)

write.table(
  change_region,
  file = con,
  row.names = FALSE,
  quote = FALSE
)


# Linear model
writeLines(
  c(
    "",
    "",
    "------------------------------------------------------------",
    "REGION-ADJUSTED LINEAR MODEL",
    "------------------------------------------------------------"
  ),
  con
)

capture.output(
  summary(linear_model_region),
  file = con,
  append = TRUE
)


# AIC comparison
writeLines(
  c(
    "",
    "",
    "------------------------------------------------------------",
    "LINEAR VS THRESHOLD MODEL COMPARISON",
    "------------------------------------------------------------"
  ),
  con
)

aic_compare_region <- AIC(
  linear_model_region,
  best_model_region
)

# Count the estimated breakpoint as one additional parameter
aic_compare_region$df[2] <- aic_compare_region$df[2] + 1
aic_compare_region$AIC[2] <- aic_compare_region$AIC[2] + 2

write.table(
  aic_compare_region,
  file = con,
  row.names = TRUE,
  quote = FALSE
)

writeLines(
  c(
    "",
    paste(
      "AIC improvement (linear - threshold) =",
      aic_compare_region$AIC[1] -
        aic_compare_region$AIC[2]
    ),
    "",
    paste(
      "N =",
      nobs(best_model_region)
    )
  ),
  con
)


close(con)

```


## 11. Optional ordered beta sensitivity analysis

Set `run_beta_sensitivity <- TRUE` below to run this section. Ordered beta regression retains exact zero and one proportions without clipping or transformation. This section does not change the primary models above. Both sensitivity models use identical observations and complete calendar-year factor levels, preserving elapsed-year gaps in the AR(1) structure.

The Gaussian model estimates additive changes in land-cover proportions, while the within-transect AR(1) component represents temporal persistence. The ordered beta sensitivity model checks dependence on the response distribution. Its coefficients and regional salinity slopes are on the logit scale and must not be compared numerically with Gaussian proportion-scale slopes. AIC values are recorded within each model only; this section does not use cross-family AIC to select a response distribution.

Suggested Methods wording after running the analysis: “We used Gaussian mixed-effects models to estimate additive changes in land-cover proportions and a within-transect AR(1) component to represent temporal persistence; sensitivity to the bounded response distribution, including exact zero and one values, was assessed with ordered beta mixed-effects models using the same fixed effects and grouping structure.” Report agreement or disagreement only after reviewing the exported results. This check does not alone resolve uncertainty associated with a near-unit AR(1) estimate.

```{r optional-beta-sensitivity}
run_beta_sensitivity <- TRUE

if (run_beta_sensitivity) {
  if (!exists("mixed_data")) stop("Run the mixed-model data preparation first.")
  if (!"ordbeta" %in% getNamespaceExports("glmmTMB")) {
    stop("This glmmTMB installation lacks ordbeta(); update glmmTMB before running this optional section.")
  }

  sensitivity_dir <- "/Users/bz294/Documents/WhiteZone/Figure/Backup/Mark_Down"
  dir.create(sensitivity_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

  sensitivity_data <- as.data.frame(mixed_data)
  sensitivity_formula <- proportion_Int2 ~
    salinity_c * region + year_c * region +
    (1 | ID) + (1 | RegionYear) + ar1(year_f + 0 | ID)

  sensitivity_families <- list(
    Gaussian = gaussian(),
    Ordered_beta = glmmTMB::ordbeta(link = "logit")
  )
  sensitivity_slopes <- list()
  sensitivity_diagnostics <- list()
  sensitivity_models <- list()

  for (zone in c("DZ", "VZ")) {
    response_name <- if (zone == "DZ") "proportion_Int2" else "proportion_Int1"
    required <- c(response_name, "salinity_c", "year_c", "year", "region", "ID")
    dat_sensitivity <- sensitivity_data[
      complete.cases(sensitivity_data[, required]), , drop = FALSE
    ]
    if (!nrow(dat_sensitivity)) stop("No complete observations for ", zone)
    if (any(dat_sensitivity[[response_name]] < 0 |
            dat_sensitivity[[response_name]] > 1)) {
      stop("Response values outside [0,1] for ", zone)
    }
    dat_sensitivity$ID <- factor(dat_sensitivity$ID)
    dat_sensitivity$region <- factor(
      dat_sensitivity$region, levels = c("West", "Central", "East")
    )
    dat_sensitivity$RegionYear <- interaction(
      dat_sensitivity$region, dat_sensitivity$year, drop = TRUE
    )
    dat_sensitivity$year_f <- factor(
      dat_sensitivity$year,
      levels = seq(min(dat_sensitivity$year), max(dat_sensitivity$year))
    )
    zone_formula <- sensitivity_formula
    zone_formula[[2]] <- as.name(response_name)

    for (model_name in names(sensitivity_families)) {
      model_key <- paste(zone, model_name, sep = "_")
      fit_warnings <- character()
      fit <- tryCatch(
        withCallingHandlers(
          glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
            zone_formula,
            data = dat_sensitivity,
            family = sensitivity_families[[model_name]],
            REML = FALSE
          ),
          warning = function(w) {
            fit_warnings <<- c(fit_warnings, conditionMessage(w))
            invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
          }
        ),
        error = function(e) e
      )
      if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
        writeLines(
          c(paste("Model:", model_key), paste("ERROR:", conditionMessage(fit))),
          file.path(sensitivity_dir, paste0(model_key, "_sensitivity_results.txt"))
        )
        warning("Sensitivity model failed: ", model_key,
                "; see its exported error file.")
        next
      }
      sensitivity_models[[model_key]] <- fit
      fit_ok <- isTRUE(fit$sdr$pdHess) && isTRUE(fit$fit$convergence == 0)
      diagnostic <- data.frame(
        zone = zone, model = model_name, N = nobs(fit),
        zeros = sum(dat_sensitivity[[response_name]] == 0),
        ones = sum(dat_sensitivity[[response_name]] == 1),
        convergence_code = fit$fit$convergence,
        positive_definite_Hessian = isTRUE(fit$sdr$pdHess),
        usable_convergence = fit_ok,
        AIC = AIC(fit),
        warnings = paste(unique(fit_warnings), collapse = " | ")
      )
      sensitivity_diagnostics[[model_key]] <- diagnostic
      slope_output <- "Slopes not reported because convergence checks failed."
      if (fit_ok) {
        slope_object <- emmeans::emtrends(fit, ~ region, var = "salinity_c")
        slope_table <- as.data.frame(summary(slope_object, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)))
        slope_table$zone <- zone
        slope_table$model <- model_name
        slope_table$scale <- if (model_name == "Gaussian") {
          "proportion per PSU"
        } else {
          "logit per PSU"
        }
        sensitivity_slopes[[model_key]] <- slope_table
        slope_output <- capture.output(print(slope_table, row.names = FALSE))
      }
      writeLines(
        c(
          paste("Model:", model_key),
          "Ordered beta retains exact 0 and 1 values unchanged.",
          "Calendar-year levels include all intervening years.",
          "Convergence diagnostics",
          capture.output(print(diagnostic, row.names = FALSE)),
          "Model summary", capture.output(summary(fit)),
          "Variance components and AR(1) correlation", capture.output(VarCorr(fit)),
          "Regional salinity slopes", slope_output,
          "Session information", capture.output(sessionInfo())
        ),
        file.path(sensitivity_dir, paste0(model_key, "_sensitivity_results.txt"))
      )
    }
  }
  if (length(sensitivity_diagnostics)) {
    write.csv(
      do.call(rbind, sensitivity_diagnostics),
      file.path(sensitivity_dir, "beta_sensitivity_diagnostics.csv"),
      row.names = FALSE
    )
  }
  if (length(sensitivity_slopes)) {
    write.csv(
      do.call(rbind, sensitivity_slopes),
      file.path(sensitivity_dir, "beta_sensitivity_regional_salinity_slopes.csv"),
      row.names = FALSE
    )
  }
  message("Sensitivity outputs saved to: ", sensitivity_dir)
}
```
